learning_objective: 🎯 Transform everyday scraps into masterpieces! Learn how to build textures and images by assembling small pieces of varied materials.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Derived from the French word 'coller' (to glue), collage is an art technique where pieces of paper, photographs, fabric, and other everyday materials are glued onto a flat surface to create a new image.
When an artist combines different materials (like painting, magazine clippings, and cloth) in a single artwork, it is called mixed media. It adds incredible physical texture and depth.
Mosaic is an ancient art form that creates images or patterns by assembling small colored pieces of hard materials like stone, tile, or glass. These small pieces are called 'tesserae'.

Both collage and mosaic rely heavily on texture. Ripped paper edges, shiny magazine pages, rough fabrics, and glossy tiles give the artwork a tactile (touchable) quality that paint alone cannot achieve.
Collage is a brilliant way to recycle and upcycle waste materials (old newspapers, wrappers, broken tiles) into something beautiful and meaningful.

fun_activity.title: 📰 The Magazine Portrait
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a large, simple outline of a face on a thick sheet of paper. Instead of coloring it, rip old magazines into small pieces sorted by color. Glue the colored paper scraps inside your outline to 'paint' the portrait!

exam_tips: 📌 Remember the origin of the word Collage: it comes from the French word 'coller' which means 'to glue'.
📌 Differentiate between Collage (uses soft, varied materials like paper/cloth) and Mosaic (uses hard materials like glass/stone).
📌 Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque were famous for using collage in the Cubist art movement.
quick_recap: ⭐ Mosaics are often used in architecture, decorating floors, walls, and ceilings in historical buildings.
⭐ 'Tesserae' is the technical term for the small pieces of stone or glass used in mosaics.
⭐ Collage allows artists to combine unrelated images to create surreal and imaginative compositions.
